gaps.sentence: They managed ___ the deadline despite the strike.
She would rather ___ at home tonight.
gaps.explanation: 'Would rather do' — the bare infinitive follows.

gaps.sentence: I really can't afford ___ on holiday this year.
gaps.explanation: afford takes the to-infinitive: can't afford to go.

gaps.sentence: I can't stand ___ kept waiting when I have an appointment.
gaps.explanation: 'Can't stand' takes a gerund; the passive gerund is 'being kept'.

gaps.sentence: She made her son ___ his room before dinner.
gaps.explanation: make + object + bare infinitive: made him tidy (passive takes to: was made to tidy).

gaps.sentence: She's considering ___ the flat and moving to the coast.
The burglar admitted ___ through the kitchen window.
gaps.explanation: 'Admit' is followed by a gerund: admitted climbing.
